deepDives.title: Peso rebounds to P63.665:$1 as oil eases slightly
deepDives.summary: The Philippine peso rebounded against the US dollar on Thursday, buoyed by the slight drop in global crude oil prices.
reasons: reader relevance 3/3: Peso level moves affect remittance value for families

article.text:
The Philippine peso rebounded against the US dollar on Thursday, buoyed by the slight drop in global crude oil prices.
The local currency gained 4.5 centavos to close at P63.665:$1 from Wednesday’s finish of P63.71:$1.
Thursday’s appreciation comes as global crude oil US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures for delivery next month fell by 0.31% to $83 per barrel as of 04:55 GMT.
“The US dollar/peso exchange rate corrected slightly lower… after slightly lower global crude oil prices,” Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. (RCBC) chief economist Michael Ricafort said in a mobile message.
Peso claws back P62-to-$1 level on lower oil prices
“[This] led to the sharp rollback in the local fuel pump prices that could help ease inflationary pressures and could also help fundamentally reduce the country’s oil import bill, trade deficit, current account deficit, and balance of payments deficit than otherwise; leading to stronger peso exchange rate vs. the US dollar,” he added.
Local equities, meanwhile, closed in the red as the Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) shed 33.93 points, or 0.62%, to 5,477.91 at the closing bell. The broader All Shares index fell by 20.6 points or 0.66% to 3,079.09.
Nearly all sectoral indices closed lower—financials by 0.55%, holding firms by 0.53%, property by 0.07%, services by 1.44%, and mining and oil by 2.69%. The industrial index gained 0.12%.
More than 675.948 million shares, valued at P6.363 billion, changed hands. Decliners led advancers, 120 to 66, while 51 issues were unchanged.

deepDives.title: US gov't eyes ending PERM green card process for Filipino nurses, physical therapists
deepDives.summary: Filipino nurses and physical therapists seeking US green cards could face additional steps and longer waiting periods under the proposed changes to the permanent labor certification program, commonly known as PERM.
reasons: reader relevance 3/3: Proposed US green card changes affecting Filipino nurses

article.text:
NEW YORK — Filipino nurses and physical therapists seeking US green cards could face additional steps and longer waiting periods under the proposed changes to the permanent labor certification program, commonly known as PERM.
In a 107-page proposal published in the Federal Register, the US Department of Labor seeks to expand the recruitment requirements employers must meet before sponsoring foreign workers for permanent residency. The department says the changes would protect US workers' wages and give qualified applicants a better chance of filling available jobs.
One major change would eliminate Schedule A, which allows employers hiring foreign nurses, physical therapists and certain individuals with exceptional ability to bypass the usual PERM recruitment process. Schedule A reflects the department's determination that too few qualified US workers are available in those occupations or categories.
Under the proposal, employers sponsoring nurses and physical therapists would have to recruit US workers and obtain labor certification from the department before filing immigrant petitions.
Employers would generally have to advertise job openings for at least 90 days and document their recruitment efforts.
For Filipino applicants, that could mean waiting longer for their potential employers to file immigrant petitions. Exactly how much time the requirements would add to individual cases remains uncertain.
If an able, willing, qualified and available US worker applies for the job, the employer may be unable to obtain the labor certification needed to sponsor a foreign applicant.
Filipino American job seekers and Filipino permanent residents could benefit from expanded recruitment requirements and safeguards for workers affected by layoffs.
Arvin Amatorio, an immigration attorney and the mayor of Bergenfield, New Jersey, said he supports electronic filing and giving US workers a fair chance at available jobs.
He warned, however, that eliminating Schedule A could make it harder for hospitals and nursing homes in underserved communities to fill vacancies.
"What concerns me most is getting rid of Schedule A. If that happens, employers sponsoring nurses and physical therapists would generally have to go through the regular recruitment process," Amatorio said in a message.
"Think about a hospital or nursing home in an underserved community that's already struggling to hire nurses. How much longer will it take to fill those jobs? It could be catastrophic for them," he added.
Amatorio also said Filipino nurses could still pursue green cards through their employers, but the longer waiting periods and higher costs could discourage some employers from sponsoring them.
"I'd rather see the Labor Department look at where the shortages actually are and keep the exemption in those areas," he added. "We can give US workers a fair shot and still make sure patients get the care they need."
The public can comment on the proposal until January 19, 2027. The Labor Department must review the comments before issuing any final rule. If issued, a final rule would set an effective date and explain how the changes would apply. Schedule A remains available under current rules.
Separately, US Department of Labor Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito said in a media interview that his office is investigating major companies over alleged abuse of foreign-worker visa programs.
D'Esposito accused some employers of hiring foreign workers while overlooking qualified Americans. He said the Trump administration, working with Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling, wants to give American workers the first chance at available jobs.
"It's not anti-immigration, it's putting American workers first," he said, rejecting accusations that the administration's approach is racist or anti-immigrant. — VDV, GMA News

deepDives.title: UBS sees limited room for monetary easing
deepDives.summary: WITH the likelihood of having limited room for monetary easing next year, international bank UBS said that the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) may still hike key policy rates totaling 50 basis points (bps) next year amid inflation pressures.In its latest Economic Outlook for the Philippines, UBS Investment Bank Research said the central bank could deliver another 25-basis-point hike in December…
reasons: reader relevance 2/3: Analysis of possible BSP rate hikes affecting loans

article.text:
WITH the likelihood of having limited room for monetary easing next year, international bank UBS said that the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) may still hike key policy rates totaling 50 basis points (bps) next year amid inflation pressures.
In its latest Economic Outlook for the Philippines, UBS Investment Bank Research said the central bank could deliver another 25-basis-point hike in December, followed by an additional 25-basis-point increase in the first quarter of next year.
This would bring the policy rate at 6.0 percent, with the bank expecting a limited room for monetary easing in 2027.
“We expect limited scope for easing in 2027, with easing only under way in 2028,” UBS said.
The BSP’s policymaking Monetary Board has raised key policy rates by a cumulative 125 bps since it started implementing a 25-bp hike in April to tame inflation.
Consumer price growth hit 7.8 percent in October due to higher transport and fuel costs.
UBS said the central bank could still hike interest rates with growth likely to rebound next year.
“Philippines is one of only two Asean economies where we expect growth to strengthen next year,” UBS said.
It expects the economy to grow by 5.1 percent next year, a significant improvement from the current 2.1-percent growth print recorded in the third quarter of this year. This is also within the 5.0- to 6.0-percent target of the government for the period.
“The improvement should be driven primarily by a recovery in public investment,” UBS said.
Since public construction accounts for roughly a quarter of investment, “this would imply an approximately 12-percentage-point swing in investment growth over 2026–2027 from public construction alone.”
“The government had already begun mobilizing funds and awarding infrastructure contracts in 2026, providing scope for projects to restart under tighter accountability mechanisms,” UBS said.
“The Philippines already has an established semiconductor industry, concentrated in backend assembly, testing and packaging, providing a manufacturing base that may eventually see more spillover benefits from a stronger global technology cycle,” it added.

MANILA, Philippines — Motorcycle-for-hire platform JoyRide PH has confirmed that its database has been exposed to a breach, asking customers to tighten security measures to avoid falling for any scams.
In a statement, JoyRide disclosed that it has become the target of a cybersecurity attack, resulting in the compromise of certain data within the app.
JoyRide said it has notified state regulators about the incident, as it has also tapped cybersecurity experts to investigate the matter.
While the investigation is rolling, JoyRide said it has placed additional controls to strengthen its security protocols. It also committed that services are still safe to use.
For the meantime, JoyRide asked its customers to never share one-time passwords. The platform also warned against responding to suspicious texts with the extent of the breach still unknown.
“Once our investigation is complete, we will notify all our stakeholders directly,” JoyRide said.
“We remain committed to protecting their [stakeholders] interests and upholding the standard of service and integrity they have come to expect from JoyRide,” the company added.
Cybersecurity advocate Deep Web Konek yesterday alerted the public of an apparent data breach that hit JoyRide.
Deep Web Konek said the breach has exposed driver registration and customer profile, although details are yet to be confirmed by JoyRide. Based on initial assessment, the hackers targeted 107 distinct information field types across 24 categories.
Deep Web Konek flagged the attack as high-risk data exposure. The sensitivity of data taken may lead to financial fraud, identity theft, impersonation and phishing.
The group said records exposed in the incident include government-issued IDs, driver’s licenses, police clearances, residential addresses, vehicle registration and e-wallet information.
Similar to JoyRide’s evaluation, Deep Web Konek said it has also yet to identify the extent of the breach, as documents remain under evaluation and investigation.

article.text:
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) dropped 33.93 points, or 0.62 percent, to 5,477.91 on Thursday, its lowest close since May 2020, as investors resumed profit-taking following a two-day recovery.
Market sentiment remained cautious amid inflation concerns, peso depreciation, slowing economic growth and renewed US-Iran tensions.
The market recorded 120 decliners against 66 gainers and 51 unchanged issues, with turnover reaching P6.16 billion, excluding extraordinary block sales.
Foreign buying turned positive, led by BPI, but selective bargain-hunting failed to reverse the market's decline.
